name: Emmons Glacier
overview: Trailhead is the ranger station at White River, 4,300 ft. Walk 3.1 miles up the river valley to tree line, where Glacier Basin (about 6000 ft) offers possible camping. Next comes the crevassed Interglacier, leading up to another possible camp, Camp Curtis (8,500 ft). At the top of that ridge, lose a little height onto the Emmons Glacier and go a short way up to the usual high camp, Camp Schurman at Steamboat Prow, 9,450 ft. From there angle up and left via a 1,500 ft snow ramp, the Corridor. Higher, the slope steepens and bends right toward the bergschrund; how hard it is to cross depends on conditions. A further steep stretch precedes the summit. Descend by the ascent route.
fa: J. W. Fobes, G. James, R. O. Wells, 1884
